Yes, I think we can close this. There's no cleanup that needs a PR, so I didn't open any.

**What's on `main` now:**

| Asked for in this issue | Issues | Merged PRs |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt templates, hiding and removing tools, overrides | #52 | #56, #58 |
| `AGENTS.md` | #53, #68 | #61, #73 |
| Skills | #54 | #62 |
| pi's base system prompt (preamble, tools, rules, cwd) | #65 | #70 |
| `SYSTEM.md` / `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` | #67 | #72 |
| `thinking_level`, default `medium` | #66 | #74 |

All of them are in release 2.5.0 (#75), and CI passes on `main` (`8988e97`).

**Checks I made in this run:**
- **The system prompt is in pi's order.** The one I got for this run has the preamble, `<tools>`, `<rules>`, then this repo's `AGENTS.md` as `<project_instructions path="…">`, then `<cwd>`, then pit's sections.
- **The docs match the code.** `docs/prompts.md` lists every system prompt section in order. `docs/how-it-works.md` no longer says `AGENTS.md` is left out of the prompt. I found no stale statements about context files, thinking, or ignored prompts.

**Differences from plain `pi` that remain, on purpose:**
- **pi extensions only add model providers.** Their tools, event handlers and commands need pi's coding agent; tools come from pi-durable extensions instead. `docs/extensions.md` says so.
- **pi's settings files aren't read.** That's `settings.json` and its compaction and retry options, which have inputs or defaults here.
- **The messages are pi-action's own.** The first message is the issue/PR template, follow-ups add the reply reminder, and there are working-tree restore notes.
- **Context files are read only up to the workspace root.** On fork PRs they come from the base branch.

**Housekeeping, if you want it:**
- **#55 (Images) is still open**, although #71 is merged and my last reply there said it's ready to close.
- **25 old branches are still on the remote.** 22 of them belong to merged PRs (for example `feat/65-base-system-prompt`, `55-image-processor`), and 3 to closed PRs #11–#13. I haven't deleted them; say so if you want me to. Turning on *Settings → Automatically delete head branches* would stop new ones from piling up.
- **#76 is still open.** It's a fix that keeps the agent from starting a pi-action run inside a run, and it isn't part of this issue.
